correctness.rationale: The five nontrivial positive-genus character quotients are the elliptic double covers of the five four-subsets. The norm/pullback composites are [8] on matching factors and zero between distinct characters (some group element fixes one quotient and acts by -1 on the other's Jacobian). The 2-primary isogeny therefore transfers the 7-divisible group and all three claimed invariants. The cubic Legendre Hasse polynomial has exactly the roots 2,4,6. Two harmonic quartets force the five points into the prime field after normalizing their common triple; complementing and applying triple transitivity reduces all prime-field configurations to one, with exactly three harmonic quartets. The rational chart therefore has 20 triple incidences as distinct points, and the single-quartet incidence total is 15(q-3), with each of the 20 points contributing three. Subtracting these contributions and then subtracting from (q-2)(q-3) proves the extension formulas. Independent finite checks give rank counts (20,0,0) over F7 and (20,630,1512) over F49, in rank order 2,4,5; the latter supplies all three cases. The general proof is not an inference from the two tests.
residual_risks: Counts are of ordered normalized marked parameters; not counts of curves up to isomorphism.

value.rationale: The rank gap and marked family are mathematically well motivated. As a separate contribution, however, the frozen classification is subsumed by the complete arrangement: counting punctured components and subtracting their known rational triple points yields every numerical entry, and elliptic slope addition yields the polygon. Printing those deductions does not supply a distinct research result.
residual_risks: The verdict is about an independent contribution beyond verified coverage, not about the usefulness of the arrangement or correctness of the numbers.
